ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the attached figure, on the left there are two rectangular function blocks labeled “1”, respectively receiving inputs A and B; each of the output terminals of these two left-side blocks has a small circle, indicating output inversion. Their outputs are connected to the AND gate function block on the right labeled “&”; the output terminal of the right-side “&” block also has a small circle, indicating that the AND gate output is inverted again, that is, NAND output, labeled Y. Reasoning: The two left-side blocks with output inversion circles respectively give ¬A and ¬B. The right-side “&” block with an output inversion circle indicates first ANDing the two inputs and then inverting, so Y = ¬(¬A · ¬B). By De Morgan’s law, Y = A + B. The OR gate A + B outputs 0 only when A=0 and B=0. Therefore, there is only 1 kind of A, B input combination that makes Y=0.

method.method_draft: From the image, identify the two left blocks as inverters on A and B because of the output bubbles, and identify the right '&' block with an output bubble as a NAND. Write the circuit as Y = ¬(¬A · ¬B). Apply De Morgan's law to simplify to Y = A + B. Since A OR B equals 0 only for A=0, B=0, the number of input combinations making Y=0 is 1.
